title: Go SDK: response envelope mappers, streaming ergonomics, and retry observability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Deliver a set of Go SDK primitives that make it ergonomic to decode strongly-typed structured responses from Redwood inference endpoints (both streaming and non-streaming), expose a small generics-based mapping layer for response envelopes, and surface retry/attempt telemetry for observability and debugging.

Background:
Current clients and internal SDK helpers are spread across multiple helper packages with ad-hoc conventions for: envelope shapes, streaming chunk decoding, error propagation, and retry counting. This causes duplicated work in downstream apps when they need typed structs and when they must reconcile partial streaming payloads into a final typed object. We want a unified approach that: (1) supports T-typed mappers (generic), (2) composes nicely with streaming consumers, (3) preserves partial-state for observability, and (4) emits retry metrics and last-error annotations on the final result.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Introduce EnvelopeMapper[T any] (package: sdk/mapper) — a tiny generic that maps a raw response envelope into a typed Go struct T and validates required fields. It returns typed result + list of warnings.
- StreamingAdapter (package: sdk/stream) — a combinator that consumes token/fragment events and uses an incremental decoder to build the typed T while supporting cancellation, backpressure and intermittent errors.
- RetryTelemetry middleware (package: sdk/middleware) — attaches attempt count, last_error, and per-attempt timing to the final response object and to the SDK telemetry events.
- Example helpers: FromJSON[T], FromAnnotatedStruct[T], and FromEnvelopeField[T] — convenience constructors for common variants.

API sketches (short):
- type EnvelopeMapper[T any] func(ctx context.Context, raw map[string]any) (T, []string, error)
- func FromJSON[T any](schema Validator) EnvelopeMapper[T]
- type StreamDecoder[T any] interface {
    PushChunk(ctx context.Context, chunk []byte) error
    Result() (T, bool, error) // bool == complete
  }

Acceptance criteria:
- New mapper and streaming adapter are implemented and covered by unit tests (>=70% on new packages).
- Backwards-compatible: existing sdk response helpers remain functional via small adapters.
- Example: README + 2 examples showing (a) non-streaming typed decode; (b) streaming decode with retry and telemetry; both compile in CI.
- Telemetry: emitted metrics include attempts:int, last_error:string (optional), decode_warnings:list.

Non-goals:
- Full schema-driven codegen. We'll rely on runtime validators and small annotation helpers; codegen work is a follow-up.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Using generics simplifies consumer code but increases surface area of exported APIs; keep primitives minimal to avoid long-term maintenance costs.
- Incremental streaming parsing must be defensive to avoid holding unbounded state for very long streams; we will enforce per-request size limits and expose early-fail hooks.
- Validator complexity: prefer composition of small validators instead of large reflective validators to keep performance predictable.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for EnvelopeMapper with positive/negative cases and warnings.
- Integration test: mock Redwood streaming endpoint that emits a structured envelope in three chunks; SDK must produce typed result and emit attempts telemetry when transient HTTP 503 is simulated.
- Fuzz test for incremental decoder to ensure it fails fast on corrupted chunks.

2026-03-08 - Li Chen: Design review: suggested exposing lightweight context keys for attempt metadata to avoid changing existing response types. Also recommended 'decode_warnings' be a string slice in telemetry payloads (not a JSON blob).

2026-03-10 - QA (Theresa Gomez): Ran integration against staging runner. Found an edge case where streaming chunks with trailing commas caused JSON incremental parser to fail; added mitigation to trim incremental buffers between fragments. Filed follow-up test (ENG-47102).
